attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The remaining gap is analytic, not linear algebraic: derive the boundary OPE factor B for reflected Wilson hairpins and prove Schur-preimage positivity for all realized finite Wilson matrices, or exhibit an actual realized triple with negative D_3 after division by B.
steps: Start with regulated reflection positivity: for every cutoff and fixed collar width delta, the finite OS matrix S_{a,L}(Theta T_delta F_i,T_delta F_j) is positive.
Use the RG-to-OS closed-cone passage to obtain a positive fixed-collar continuum matrix N^delta(F), then pass delta down to the reflection plane where the collar limit exists.

Model the collar collapse by a boundary OPE N=B circ M + A. Diagonal trace continuity gives A_{ii}=0. If A is a positive contact matrix, Cauchy-Schwarz gives A_{ij}=0, so the additive contact vanishes.

The intended same-theory target matrix is therefore M=B^{[-1]} circ N. Thus the exact bridge condition is not positivity of N alone, but positivity of this Schur preimage for every realized locked Wilson family.
For two observables the condition reduces to the valid threshold |N_{12}|/sqrt(N_{11}N_{22}) <= |B_{12}|/sqrt(B_{11}B_{22}).

For three observables, pairwise thresholds do not decide positivity. The normalized determinant D_3 detects boundary triangle phase and correlation defects; a negative D_3 is a concrete same-theory falsifier even when every two-by-two minor is nonnegative.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite Schur-preimage criterion is valid, but the Yang-Mills construction has not yet shown that the Wilson collar algebra realizes a sufficiently rich family of N matrices, nor that the boundary anomaly B has the required rank-one or preimage-positive structure.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: finite Schur-preimage obstruction

assumptions: For each fixed collar width delta>0, T_delta F_i has support strictly in t>0 and S_{a,L} is reflection positive on the regulated lattice/continuum cutoff theory.
The cutoff-removal topology controls every mixed reflected matrix entry S_{a,L}(Theta T_delta F_i,T_delta F_j), not only individual Wilson expectations.
The collar collapse has a boundary OPE of the form N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}+A_{ij}, with B_{ij} nonzero on the finite family under test.
Diagonal trace continuity is valid; if A is a positive additive contact matrix, A_{ii}=0 forces A=0 by Cauchy-Schwarz.
The matrix family N(F) is the realized cone supplied by the locked Yang-Mills Wilson algebra, not the full cone of all abstract positive matrices.
definitions: source object: finite collar OS matrices N(F) obtained from regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms S_{a,L}(Theta T_delta F_i,T_delta F_j) on the locked positive-time gauge-invariant Wilson/composite algebra.

target object: intended continuum same-theory OS matrices M(F)=S(Theta F_i,F_j) on the same labeled observables, before adding boundary counterterms or changing Wilson-loop renormalization at the reflection plane.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions by passing fixed-collar positive matrices to N(F), then proving the boundary trace correction sends N(F) to a positive M(F).

same-theory condition: the observable labels F_i, gauge-invariant test algebra, and Wilson renormalization convention are identical before and after collar collapse; any boundary factor B must be a removable congruence or a Schur-preimage-positive defect, not a hidden change of theory.

equations.label: fixed-collar closed cone
equations.latex: N^{\delta}_{ij}(F)=\lim_{a,L} S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j),\qquad N^\delta(F)\succeq 0
equations.valid_when: The RG compactness topology is strong enough for all finite reflected collar probes.

equations.label: boundary factorization
equations.valid_when: The reflected Wilson collar collapse admits a multiplicative boundary factor plus an additive contact term.

equations.label: same-theory Schur preimage
equations.valid_when: OS positivity is being claimed for the intended target observables, not for a boundary-renormalized algebra.

equations.label: three-point determinant test
equations.valid_when: M is normalized to M_{ii}=1; this condition is required in addition to all 2-by-2 principal minors.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A realized triple with normalized N_{12}=N_{23}=0.45, N_{13}=-0.45 and normalized B_{12}=B_{23}=B_{13}=0.5 is an algebraic falsifier: N is positive and all pairwise thresholds pass, but B^{[-1]} circ N has determinant 1-2(0.9)^3-3(0.9)^2<0.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the remaining positivity question from informal boundary regularity into a finite matrix preservation criterion on realized Wilson OS matrices.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Assume fixed-collar RG convergence is valid for every finite reflected gauge-invariant Wilson family and that additive reflection-plane contacts vanish after diagonal trace continuity. Then same-theory OS positivity of the target continuum functions is equivalent to positivity of the Schur preimage B(F)^{[-1]} circ N(F) for every realized finite collar OS matrix N(F). Pairwise damping inequalities are necessary but not sufficient; the first genuinely new falsifier can occur in a three-observable determinant through a boundary phase or triangle-correlation defect.

assumptions: The Wilson core is dense for the OS reconstruction topology after collaring.
Boundary factors vary continuously under small deformations of the hairpin footprints.
The realized triple cone is rich enough to test boundary phases, not merely pairwise magnitudes.
definitions: normalized anomaly beta_{ij}=B_{ij}/sqrt(B_{ii}B_{jj}) after removing diagonal one-body Wilson factors.
boundary triangle invariant: the phase/magnitude obstruction beta_{12} beta_{23} overline{beta_{13}}; it equals 1 for a pure diagonal congruence on normalized rank-one data.
rich realized cone: the set of Wilson collar OS matrices contains, or approximates strongly enough, rank-one three-observable correlation matrices with selectable relative phases.
Schur-preimage validity: for every realized positive N(F), the matrix beta(F)^{[-1]} circ N(F) remains positive.

equations.label: triangle invariant
equations.valid_when: The normalized multiplicative anomaly beta is defined and all three pair entries are nonzero.

equations.label: rank-one congruence condition
equations.valid_when: The boundary factor is only a harmless diagonal congruence after normalization.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If perturbative or constructive Wilson data show that the realized triple cone is too thin to approximate rank-one phase triples, the rank-one conclusion is not valid; the branch must keep the weaker realized Schur-preimage condition.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a promotion criterion: it explains what extra density/richness would upgrade finite Schur-preimage checking into boundary Gram triviality.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the locked Wilson collar algebra is rich enough to realize normalized three-point OS correlation patterns arbitrarily close to every rank-one phase triple, then a valid same-theory Schur-preimage bridge forces the normalized boundary anomaly to be rank-one on that core. Equivalently, every boundary triangle invariant must vanish; otherwise some realized triple supplies a determinant falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the RG topology cannot supply mixed reflected collar matrices or if the boundary OPE relation N=B circ M + A is not available even on a dense Wilson core.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves B^{[-1]} circ N is positive for every finite realized locked Wilson family, either by rank-one boundary congruence on a rich core or by direct finite-minor inequalities including all triple determinants.
control_decision.reason: The branch has produced a sharper and testable bridge lemma rather than repeating the closed-cone observation. The next work is finite-dimensional but tied to real Yang-Mills boundary OPE data, so pivoting is premature.

dependency_updates.description: The closed-cone argument remains valid for fixed-collar and collar-limit matrices N, but it does not by itself prove OS positivity for the intended target M when a boundary anomaly B relates N to M.
dependency_updates.status: partially discharged; now conditional on Schur-preimage positivity

dependency_updates.description: The algebra must be locked strongly enough to define realized finite Wilson matrices and rich enough to test three-observable boundary phase defects.
Topology must control finite mixed reflected collar entries first; separate trace/OPE estimates are needed for the reflection-plane Schur correction.
For every realized Wilson family F, B(F)^{[-1]} circ N(F) must be positive; finite determinants, beginning at triples, are the concrete tests.
Need an analytic computation or bound for multiplicative boundary factors B_{ij} generated when reflected Wilson collars collide at t=0.

falsifiers: A three-hairpin Wilson family for which N(F) is positive but det(B^{[-1]} circ N(F))<0 is a decisive same-theory falsifier.
A boundary OPE with nonzero additive contact after diagonal trace continuity would falsify the reduction to the multiplicative Schur-preimage problem.
A cutoff-removal topology that controls single Wilson loop limits but not mixed reflected entries S(Theta F_i,F_j) falsifies the claimed valid RG-to-OS interface.
A boundary factor B with zeros where the realized collar matrix N has nonzero entries is a falsifier for entrywise same-theory reconstruction.
A proof that only all two-by-two thresholds hold, with no finite determinant control, is not valid for full OS positivity because triple phase obstructions can remain.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 198 shows that the branch must not promote from pairwise damping tests to OS positivity. The valid condition is finite Schur-preimage positivity on the realized Wilson cone, and the first phase-sensitive falsifier is a three-hairpin determinant. This sharpens the obstruction from a vague nonrank-one boundary Gram factor to an explicit matrix experiment: compute B and N for triples, then test det(B^{[-1]} circ N).
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out the smallest reflected Wilson hairpin triple near the reflection plane: compute or bound the normalized boundary anomaly beta_{ij}, estimate the realized collar correlations N_{ij}, and evaluate the three-point determinant D_3(B^{[-1]} circ N) as the next concrete falsifier test.
